faq: Can customers keep their old passwords?
In almost every case, no. Platforms store passwords in a form that cannot be exported or imported. Customers get a short email with a link to set a new one, and we write that email with you.
How do you handle privacy and consent?

Only customers who agreed to marketing are marked as subscribed in the new store. We keep the consent date where the platform stores it, and follow data protection rules that apply to you, such as GDPR.
Do you keep a copy of my customer data?
No. We work through files and access inside your accounts, and we delete any working files from our systems once the job is finished. We never resell or reuse customer data.
What about guest customers who never made an account?
They are imported as customer records with their order details where the new platform allows, but they will not have login accounts. We note this in the report so you can plan your messaging.

desc:
Customer account migration for online stores means moving your shoppers, their addresses and their email consent from the old platform to the new one. Ecom Swift LLC handles the export, cleanup and import in your own account, so your customer base arrives intact.

## What is customer account migration?

Customer account migration is the process of exporting the people who have bought from you or signed up to your store, and loading their records into a new store. A record usually holds a name, an email address, one or more shipping addresses, tags, notes and a marketing consent flag. Done well, a returning shopper can find their details waiting for them. Done badly, you lose contacts, create duplicates or email people who asked you to stop.

## Why the customer list is worth protecting

Your customer list is the cheapest source of sales you own. A returning shopper already trusts you, knows your products and does not need to be won over again. If the list is lost or damaged in a move, you pay to reach those people a second time through ads.

Trust matters too. Shoppers who opted out of email expect that choice to be respected on the new platform. A migration that resets everyone to "subscribed" can cause complaints and damage your sender reputation.

## How it affects repeat sales and support

Accounts shape the shopping experience after the move. When addresses are present, checkout is quicker for returning customers. When tags and notes survive, your support team still sees who is a wholesale buyer or had a special arrangement. When segments are rebuilt, your first campaign on the new store can target the right people on day one.

Passwords are the one thing most platforms will not move, because they are stored in a form that cannot be read or transferred. That is normal and expected. The practical answer is a clear invite message that asks each customer to set a new password, which is why testing that message matters as much as the data.

## What a good customer migration includes

- A clean export from the old platform, with every field you need mapped to the right field on the new one.
- Duplicate emails merged before import, so nobody appears twice.
- Names, addresses and phone numbers formatted to the rules of the new platform.
- Email marketing consent status carried over, so opt-outs stay opted out.
- Tags, notes and customer groups mapped to the closest equivalent.
- An account invite email that explains the change in plain words and links to a password setup page.
- A test import on a small sample before the full list is loaded.
- Handling for guest buyers who never created an account.
- A report listing any record that was skipped and the reason.

## What we do

We start by exporting your customers from the old store and reading the file for problems: blank emails, badly formed addresses, repeated people and unusual characters. We fix what can be fixed safely and list what cannot.

Next we match each column to a field on the new store and import a small sample. We open those records, check that the data landed where it should and test the invite email with a few real accounts. Only then do we load the full list.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many customers are moved and how much is carried across. Larger packages add consent status, tags, rebuilt segments, a reminder for people who have not activated their account and a closing report. Balances such as store credit or gift cards are noted and moved where the new platform allows it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Export a fresh copy of your list on the day you plan to import it.
- Keep the original file untouched as a backup.
- Tell customers in advance that a new store and a password reset are coming.
- Check your consent records before the first email goes out.
- Decide how long you will keep inactive contacts.

**Avoid:**
- Importing everyone as subscribed to save time.
- Merging two lists without removing repeated emails first.
- Promising that old passwords will work.
- Sending the invite email from an address customers do not recognize.
- Importing test data into the live customer list.

## Who this is for

A store owner changing platforms who has years of customers and does not want to start from zero. A brand that has outgrown its first platform and wants a tidy list on the new one. A seller merging two shops into one, who needs the duplicates sorted out before they cause confusion.

## What we need from you

Send us the customer export or let us create it from the old store, plus a note on any groups or tags that matter to you. We also need your preferred wording for the account invite, or we will draft it for you to approve.

We never need your passwords. Access is given as a staff or collaborator user in the stores involved, and you can remove it whenever the work is finished. Customer data stays in your accounts, and we delete any working files once you confirm the import is correct.
